topic: Discrete Convolutions: From Image Blurring to Feature Detection

sections.title: Prerequisites & Intuition (1 min)
lecture_lines: A kernel is a small, sliding window.
Matrices store our input image data.
Convolution performs element-wise multiplication and summation.
animations: Initialize empty input grid #FFFFFF with label "Input".
Show kernel overlay on input grid and calculate element-wise product.

sections.title: The Mechanism: Sliding & Computing (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: The kernel slides over the input matrix.
We sum products within the kernel area.
This operation creates a new output matrix.
animations: Animate 3x3 kernel #FF5733 sliding across input matrix.
Highlight matching cells in input and kernel with #FFFF00 for summation.
Fade in resulting values appearing in output matrix #00FF00.

sections.title: Applications: Image Processing (1.5 min)
lecture_lines: Blur kernels average surrounding pixel values.
Kernel weights define the output image's features.
animations: Show input image matrix with color #FFFFFF.
Overlay blur kernel to average neighboring values #00FFFF.
Overlay edge-detection kernel to emphasize contrast #FF00FF.

sections.title: The Future: Feature Maps in AI (1 min)
lecture_lines: Deep learning learns these kernel values automatically.
AI uses these features to recognize objects.
Computers now see the world like humans.
animations: Animate multiple feature maps being generated in parallel #FFFFFF.
Stack feature maps into a multi-layered neural network structure.
